newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 28.

text.p: The government will pump an extra $4 million into Auckland Maori television channel Aotearoa Television Network to keep it afloat till June in a move that has led to accusations of cronyism. The Cabinet decided yesterday that the channel -- estimated to have 18,000 viewers a week -- would get $2 million from the public broadcasting fee through New Zealand on Air and $2 million directly from taxpayers. Page 1.

Justice Minister Doug Graham said on Monday he would approach government colleagues to gauge support for a bill allowing minor criminal convictions to be wiped from records after a time. A committee of Auckland lawyers published a paper on Monday calling for such convictions to be wiped from records after five years. Only those convicted under the Summary Proceedings Act or of anything carrying a sentence of less than six months' imprisonment would be eligible. Page 1.

New Zealand spent $4.2 billion more overseas than it earned in the year to September -- the worst figures in almost a decade. The current deficit was equal to 4.6 percent of gross domestic product and was higher than market predictions. The deficit is now at its worst level as a percentage of GDP since late 1987. Page 1.

Police Minister Jack Elder will investigate tougher laws against gangs in the wake of a weekend of violence. After three incidents in three days in which tensions between gangs erupted into violence, Elder said he would be likely to support laws
tougher than those proposed by the government last year. Page 2.

The Corrections Department has reinstated both prison managers suspended after three inmates smashed out of Christchurch's Papura on Friday night. The department said on Monday it had been "mutually agreed" that general manager Tony Spencer would not return to Paparua while the breakout was investigated. Instead, Spencer will act as general manager of nearby Rolleston Prison and Rolleston manager Paul Rushton will take Spencer's place. Page 2.

Proposals for an overhaul of adoption laws will soon go before Parliament, Social Welfare Department briefing papers say. The briefing papers to the government say the 1955 Adoption Act is well overdue for revision and that plans for significant reform of the act have "dragged on for too long".

The Education Ministry was confident there would be enough teachers to staff all schools as they began the first term, teacher supply manager Irene Lynch said on Monday. Most schools started on Monday, with Auckland and Northland schools beginning today after the anniversary day long weekend. Lynch said the
ministry thought there would be good coverage in Auckland, where teacher organisations have said the shortage will be worst. Page 3.

Government policies to cut immigration and increase state spending are leading to worse balance of payment figures, according to economists. A fall in immigration last year made a big dent in the latest balance of payments figures, with a deficit of $4.2 billion for the year to September. The shortfall between what we spend and earned overseas in the last September year was equal to 4.6 percent of gross domestic product, the
highest level since 1987, according to figures issued on Monday. Page 10.

Confidence among exporters and South Island manufacturers is showing a dramatic improvement, according to the latest Wespac-Trust Manufacturers' quarterly survey. With Upper North Island manufacturers less pessimistic, the sector overall is slightly positive on outlook, says the survey by New Zealand Institute of Economic Research. However, "for the first time in years, industry expects its profit to be in decline at a time when confidence is improving," Manufacturers Federation chief
executive Simon Arnold said in a commentary on the survey. Page 10.

Underground Fasions managing director Barry Rissetto and his wife, Diane, are bailing out of their struggling company after 18 months of failing fortunes. In a statement to the Stock Exchange on Monday, Underground said Just Jeans Holdings was to offer 33.5 cents a share for Underground Fasions through a wholly owned subsidiary, Kimbyr Investments. Page 10.

Seafresh Holdings has declared a final, fully imputed dividend of 0.5 cents a share, taking the total for the 15 months to September 30, 1996, to one cent. The company said its recently acquired fourth deep-sea trawler, the Nan Hai, was fishing successfully after a refit last month. A contribution to profit was expected in the current year. Page 10.

A sharp fall in the value of the New Zealand dollar late last week may foreshadow a further strong correction in the currency, technical analysts said. The Kiwi's inexorable rise, which has squeezed exporters and frustrated Reserve Bank
monetary policy, may have come to an end last Thursday when it fell nearly a quarter of a US cent to US$69.84c, breaking through a four-year uptrend in a chart prepared by Bankers Trust. Page 10.

Ansett New Zealand is expected to report another profit despite high fuel costs and traffic disruptions caused by bad weather and congestion. During the past couple of years, the airline -- now wholly owned by news Ltd -- has produced two consecutive profits totalling $11 million. Page 10.
